subject: pe
source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel GCSE PE & Sport Science specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Fitness & Body Systems
units.blurb: Anatomy, movement, physical training and data (Component 1)

units.name: Health & Performance
units.blurb: Health, sport psychology, society and data (Component 2)

units.name: Practical Performance
units.blurb: Assessed performance in three physical activities (Component 3)

units.name: Personal Exercise Programme (PEP)
units.blurb: Plan, carry out and evaluate a six-to-eight-week PEP (Component 4)

topics.name: Applied Anatomy & Physiology
topics.blurb: Skeletal, muscular, cardiovascular and respiratory systems; aerobic/anaerobic exercise; short- and long-term effects

topics.name: Movement Analysis
topics.blurb: Lever systems and mechanical advantage; planes and axes of movement

topics.name: Physical Training
topics.blurb: Components of fitness, fitness testing, principles of training, injury prevention, warm-up and cool-down

topics.name: Use of Data (Component 1)
topics.blurb: Collecting, presenting and interpreting data from fitness and body-systems topics

topics.name: Health, Fitness & Wellbeing
topics.blurb: Physical, emotional and social health; sedentary lifestyle; energy use, diet, nutrition and hydration

topics.name: Sport Psychology
topics.blurb: Skill classification, goal setting and SMART targets, guidance and feedback, mental preparation

topics.name: Socio-cultural Influences
topics.blurb: Engagement patterns, commercialisation and the media, ethical and socio-cultural issues

topics.name: Use of Data (Component 2)
topics.blurb: Analysing and evaluating data on health, participation and performance

topics.name: Skills in Isolation/Unopposed
topics.blurb: Demonstrating skills and techniques unopposed across three chosen activities

topics.name: Skills in Competitive Situations
topics.blurb: Applying skills, decision-making and strategies under pressure in formal/competitive play

topics.name: Analysis & Evaluation of Performance
topics.blurb: Analysing and evaluating performance to bring about personal improvement

topics.name: Aim & Planning Analysis
topics.blurb: Analyse activity demands, run a battery of fitness tests, set the aim, SMART targets and training methods; complete a PAR-Q

topics.name: Carrying Out & Monitoring
topics.blurb: Deliver training over six to eight weeks, record sessions and adapt the programme as it progresses

topics.name: Evaluation of the PEP
topics.blurb: Compare pre- and post-PEP data, justify changes in performance and recommend further improvements

connections.why: Lever systems, planes and axes describe how the bones, joints and muscles studied in anatomy actually produce movement
Knowing how the body systems respond to exercise underpins training methods and the adaptations they cause
Heart-rate, stroke-volume and cardiac-output values are interpreted as graphical data
Fitness-test results are collected, presented and compared against normative data tables
The fitness components and exercise benefits learned in training explain how activity improves health and wellbeing
Body-system knowledge shows why a sedentary lifestyle harms health and how exercise reduces those risks
Trends in physical-health and participation issues are interpreted from graphical data
Participation, commercialisation and ethical trends are analysed from statistical data
Both topics are assessed together in the Component 2 extended-response question on performance and society
Skill classification, guidance and feedback shape how practical skills are practised and refined
Physical attributes such as strength, speed and stamina from the body systems support successful competitive performance
Psychological control of arousal, anxiety and aggression is applied when performing under pressure
Skills first secured unopposed must then be applied in full competitive situations
Competitive performance is the evidence base that is analysed and evaluated for improvement
Analysing performance weaknesses identifies the fitness component a PEP should target
The principles of training, fitness tests and training methods are the toolkit for planning the PEP
The planned aim, targets and methods are put into action and monitored across six to eight weeks
Monitoring data collected during training is what the final evaluation analyses
Data-handling skills are used to plot and interpret pre- and post-PEP fitness results
Diet, energy use and the health benefits of fitness inform a safe, effective PEP
